stem.text: Visitors enter an amusement park at the rate \( R(t) = 2 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{4} \right)} + 10 \) people per hour, where t is measured in hours for \( 0 \le t \le 5 \). The park holds 60 people at time \( t = 0 \). During the same time, visitors leave the park at the rate \( D(t) = t + 5 \) people per hour. Using a calculator, find the total number of people that arrive during the time interval \( 1 \le t \le 4 \). Show the setup, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The amount that arrives is the integral of the inflow rate over the interval, \( \int_{1}^{4} \left(2 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{4} \right)} + 10\right)\,dt \), and nothing is added for the starting amount or taken away.
With the calculator in radian mode, the integral is about 33.053 people.

options.derivation: the integral evaluated with the calculator in degree mode
the rate evaluated at the endpoints and subtracted, R(b) - R(a), in place of its integral
the amount present at the end reported, the starting amount added to the integral of the inflow
